newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan shares slip, U.S. holiday hurts trade.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan shares slip, U.S. holiday hurts trade.

text.p: Share prices on the Caracas Stock Exchange slipped in scant trade Monday with foreign investors absent due to a U.S. market holiday, brokers said.
The market's 19-share index fell 0.16 percent at 4,593.96, as 14 stocks closed lower, 10 higher and eight unchanged. Only 533 million bolivars ($1.1 million) changed hands, the exchange said.

"The slowness of the market was expected because of the holiday in the United States. When there are no foreign investors entering, local investors also back off," said Simon Brad of the Banesco brokerage.
Brokers said profit taking which started last Thursday continued but was tempered by some selective buying.

Among leading stocks, benchmark Electricidad de Caracas rose 5.00 bolivars to 391.00 bolivars, steel company Sivensa slipped 3.00 bolivars to 292.00 bolivars and textile company Mantex closed flat at 39.00 bolivars.
